sections.h2: How do you sell a house fast in Hillsborough, New Jersey?
sections.html:
Most Hillsborough owners pick one of three routes: list with an agent, sell without one, or accept a cash offer from a buyer who takes the house as-is. The township is in Somerset County, in the Raritan Valley, and its own website describes it as 52 miles from Manhattan.

Speed in Hillsborough depends less on the price you pick than on the paperwork. A smoke detector certificate, any open building permits and a clean tax record decide how soon a closing date can be set.

  • Agent listing: the widest exposure, but showings, a buyer's mortgage and a repair list all add weeks.
  • Sale by owner: you keep the commission and take on pricing, contracts and the township inspection yourself.
  • Cash buyer: no lender and no repair negotiation, so the timeline is mostly the title work and the certificate inspection.

Whichever route you take, compare the net figure after state fees and any repairs, not the headline price.

sections.h2: Where is Hillsborough and how did it develop?
sections.html:
Hillsborough Township covers 55.10 square miles, which makes it the largest of Somerset County's 21 municipalities by area. Its 54.61 square miles of land include several named communities, among them Belle Mead, Neshanic, Flagtown, Amwell and Woods Tavern.

A royal charter created the township in September 1771, and the Legislature incorporated it on February 21, 1798. Millstone split off as a borough in 1894 and Manville in 1929. Growth came mostly after 1950: the population went from 3,875 that year to 36,634 in 2000 and 43,276 in the 2020 census, according to the encyclopedia entry on the township.

Nearly 40 percent of the land is protected or preserved open space. That includes Duke Farms, a 2,700 acre estate in the northeast corner, so a house near preserved land will often have farm or woodland views that stay put.

The climate is humid subtropical. January lows average 18 degrees and July highs 85, with about 47.85 inches of precipitation a year, so a buyer's inspector will look closely at roofs, gutters and basements.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Hillsborough homes and owners?
sections.html:
Hillsborough is mostly an owner-occupied township: 79.5 percent of housing units are lived in by their owners, per the 2020 to 2024 American Community Survey estimates published in QuickFacts. Median value of an owned home is $547,600, and median monthly owner costs run $3,017 with a mortgage and $1,470 without one.

The same release counts 16,388 households averaging 2.67 people, a median household income of $154,031 and a mean commute of 33.3 minutes. About 91.1 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, a sign that few homes change hands in any one year. The July 2025 population estimate is 45,061, up 4.1 percent from the April 2020 base.

For a seller this means your likely buyer is a commuter household with a sizable income, and a listing competes with a modest supply of similar homes. A buyer who needs cash certainty or no financing contingency is a smaller group but a real one.

sections.h2: Which roads, buses and schools do buyers weigh in Hillsborough?
sections.html:
Buyers here ask about the commute and the school district before they ask about the kitchen. The facts below come from the township's entry on the public encyclopedia.

  • Roads: U.S. Route 206 is the main route. A 3.75 mile bypass finished in 2021, and the old road is meant to become a downtown main street. County Routes 514 and 533 also cross the township, while Interstate 287 sits just outside in Bridgewater and Franklin.
  • Transit: D.H.I.L.A.N. buses link to Manville, Bridgewater and Somerville, and Coach USA runs four weekday morning express trips to Midtown Manhattan. A proposed West Trenton rail line with Belle Mead and Hillsborough stops was cancelled for lack of funding.
  • Schools: the Hillsborough Township School District runs pre-kindergarten through grade 12. Its nine schools include five K to 4 elementaries, Auten Road Intermediate for grades 5 and 6, a middle school for 7 and 8 and the high school. Enrollment was 7,288 in 2020-21.

sections.h2: What paperwork does a Hillsborough seller handle before closing?
sections.html:
Four offices touch a Hillsborough sale: the Fire Safety Department, the Building Department, the Tax Collector and the Somerset County Clerk. The table lists what each one asks of the seller.

Hillsborough closing checklist, from the township Building and Tax pages and the Somerset County Clerk land records page
ItemOfficeWhat to know
Smoke detector certificationFire Safety DepartmentFor a resale, the Building Department does not issue a certificate of occupancy. Schedule this inspection instead.
Open permitsBuilding DepartmentThe current owner must close any open permit, even one pulled by a previous owner.
Quarterly taxesTax CollectorDue February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, with a grace period through the 10th.
Deed recordingSomerset County ClerkA county cover sheet goes with every deed. The first page costs $45 and each added page $10.

The township's SDL portal shows permit status and inspection results, so pull the permit history for your address early. Fixing a stale permit takes less time than explaining it to a buyer's attorney.

sections.h2: How are Hillsborough property taxes billed and what happens when you sell?
sections.html:
The township mails an estimated third-quarter bill each July, based on the current year's assessed value. The Tax Collector warns against multiplying that bill by four, because adjustments land in the third and fourth quarters.

Hillsborough runs an annual reassessment program, so assessments follow market movement from year to year. The tax rate per $100 of assessed value fell from $2.419 in 2018 to $2.143 in 2024, according to the township, even as values climbed. Payments must be received by the 10th of the due month, and postmarks do not count.

If you pay by ACH direct debit, tell the Tax Collector as soon as you list. The office says debits continue until it is notified. Anyone behind on taxes should ask the office for a payoff figure before closing; the 2026 online auction of 2025 and earlier delinquent charges closed at 8:00 am on September 23, 2026.

On appeals, the state sets April 1 as the usual filing date with the county board of taxation, and May 1 where a municipal revaluation or reassessment took place. Ask the Somerset County Board of Taxation which date fits your parcel. A further appeal to the Tax Court must be filed within 45 days of the board's judgment.

sections.h2: What does the state add to the cost of selling in Hillsborough?
sections.html:
The seller pays New Jersey's Realty Transfer Fee when the deed is recorded. For a sale above $350,000 the rate steps up by band: $2.90 per $500 on the first $150,000, $4.25 from $150,000 to $200,000, $4.80 from $200,000 to $550,000 and $5.30 from $550,000 to $850,000.

A Hillsborough seller who lives in New Jersey signs GIT/REP-3 at closing, which avoids an estimated income tax payment then. If the house was your principal residence for two of the last five years, federal rules let you exclude up to $250,000 of gain, or $500,000 on a joint return, and New Jersey follows that exclusion.

faqs.q: Do I need a certificate of occupancy to sell my Hillsborough house?
faqs.a: Not from the Building Department. The township states that it does not issue a certificate of occupancy for the resale of a residential property. You schedule a smoke detector certification inspection with the Fire Safety Department instead, and your closing attorney will say whether the buyer's lender wants anything further.

faqs.q: When are Hillsborough property taxes due?
faqs.a: February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1. The township allows a grace period through the 10th, or the next business day if the 10th falls on a weekend or holiday. Payments must be in the tax office by then because postmarks are not accepted, and interest runs back to the due date after that.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Hillsborough assessment?
faqs.a: Usually April 1, filed with the Somerset County Board of Taxation on Form A-1. The state moves the date to May 1 where a revaluation or reassessment was done. Ask the board or the township assessor which date applies to your parcel before you prepare the petition.

faqs.q: Who records the deed when I sell in Hillsborough?
faqs.a: The Somerset County Clerk. The office records deeds, mortgages and related documents, requires a county cover sheet on every filing and accepts e-recording through certified partners. A deed's first page costs $45 and each added page $10, and your title company normally handles the filing.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Hillsborough house that has open permits or needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes, though open permits travel with the property. The Building Department says the current owner must close a permit even when a previous owner did the work. A buyer who purchases as-is can take on repairs, but closing the permit first removes a common reason for a deal to stall.
